repo_overview.summary: Promptise Foundry is a Python framework (PyPI package 'promptise') for building agentic systems on top of the LangChain ecosystem, rather than a single agent application. It bundles five layers in one package: an agent builder (build_agent/PromptiseAgent) with MCP tool discovery, memory, guardrails and caching; a composable reasoning engine that executes a directed PromptGraph of typed nodes; an MCP server and client SDK with access control and middleware; an autonomous agent runtime that supervises long-running agent processes; and a prompt engineering layer with block-based token budgeting. The agentic loop lives in engine/execution.py, where PromptGraphEngine.ainvoke traverses the graph, calls the LLM at prompt nodes, executes tools, and follows conditional edges until a terminal node is reached.

resilience.name: bounded graph traversal with global and per-node iteration caps
resilience.what_it_is: The engine counts every node execution against a global cap (max_iterations, default 50) and every single node against a per-node cap (max_node_iterations, default 25). Each BaseNode additionally carries its own max_iterations (default 10, 15 for the ReAct reasoning node). Exceeding the global cap breaks the traversal loop, exceeding the per-node cap routes into stuck-node recovery.
resilience.function_in_system: Wraps the main traversal loop in PromptGraphEngine.ainvoke. Caps how long a run may continue when the model keeps requesting tools or the graph keeps cycling between nodes. Otherwise a model that never produces a tool-free final answer would loop and burn tokens until the process is killed.

resilience.name: stuck-node recovery with escalating fallback chain
resilience.what_it_is: When a node exceeds its per-node iteration limit, _handle_stuck_node picks a recovery target in three steps: the node's own "error" transition, then a graph-global __error__ node if one exists, then a forced __end__.
resilience.function_in_system: Sits at the safety check at the end of each traversal iteration in ainvoke and astream_events. Turns a stuck node into a controlled hand-off to error handling and keeps the graph author's own recovery path in charge where one is declared. Otherwise a stuck node would simply terminate the run and discard whatever recovery logic the graph declares.

resilience.name: cycle detection via visit-pattern matching

Catches oscillation between several nodes, which the plain per-node counters miss because no single node exceeds its own limit. Otherwise a two- or three-node ping-pong would run until the global iteration cap, spending a full budget on repeated work.

resilience.name: node error containment as node result
resilience.what_it_is: Every node execution is wrapped so that an escaping exception is converted into a NodeResult carrying error="<ExcType>: <message>" instead of propagating. The same conversion happens in the streaming path, where a failed stream additionally falls back to a plain execute() call.
resilience.function_in_system: Sits directly around node.execute inside the traversal loop of ainvoke. Makes a node failure a routable state of the graph rather than the end of the run, which is the precondition for on_error edges, SKIP_ON_ERROR and stuck-node recovery to work at all. Otherwise any exception in any node would abort the whole invocation and discard the accumulated state.

resilience.name: declarative error routing via conditional edges
resilience.what_it_is: PromptGraph offers edge constructors whose conditions read failure-related NodeResult fields: on_error fires when result.error is set, on_guard_fail fires when result.guards_failed is non-empty, and on_confidence fires when the structured output's confidence reaches a threshold. _resolve_transition evaluates these conditions in priority order and catches exceptions raised by a condition itself.
resilience.function_in_system: Sits in the transition resolution step after each node execution. Lets the graph author express recovery topology (retry path, repair node, human escalation) as part of the graph rather than as branching code inside nodes. Otherwise error handling would have to be re-implemented inside every node, and a failed node would fall through to its default_next as if it had succeeded.

resilience.name: node retry with capped exponential backoff and error feedback
resilience.what_it_is: A node marked RETRYABLE is executed up to node.max_iterations times with backoff min(0.5 * 2^attempt, 8.0) seconds between attempts. Before each further attempt the engine writes _retry_attempt and _retry_error into state.context so the node can adapt its prompt to the previous failure, and clears those keys on success or exhaustion. RetryNode implements the same scheme as an explicit wrapper around another node, additionally recording _retry_node.
resilience.function_in_system: Sits between the traversal loop and node.execute, inside a single graph step. Absorbs transient failures (provider errors, tool timeouts, malformed model output) before they become a node error that has to be routed. The error feedback into state.context turns a blind repeat into an informed second attempt. Otherwise every transient provider hiccup would surface as a node failure and consume the graph's error-handling path.

        result = await node.execute(state, config)
        if not result.error:
            # Success — clean up retry context

            state.context.pop("_retry_error", None)

            iteration=state.iteration,
            error=last_error,

resilience.name: skip-on-error flag
resilience.what_it_is: A node carrying NodeFlag.SKIP_ON_ERROR is not executed when the previous node in state.node_history finished with an error. The engine returns a synthetic NodeResult with transition_reason="skipped_on_error" and the traversal continues.
resilience.function_in_system: Runs in _pre_execute_flags, before the node executes. The counterpart to CRITICAL: it keeps the graph alive past an optional step whose input is already broken. Otherwise a node would run on missing input and add a second, misleading failure on top of the original one.

resilience.name: tool-call failure containment and feedback
resilience.what_it_is: Each tool call is executed inside _exec_one_tool, which turns an unknown tool name and any tool exception into an "Error: ..." string marked success=False. Multiple calls run concurrently via asyncio.gather(..., return_exceptions=True), where a raised exception is also converted into an error record, and results are appended in the original order to keep tool_call_id alignment. Every outcome becomes a ToolMessage in state.messages plus an observation, and failures increment result.tool_calls_failed.
resilience.function_in_system: Sits inside PromptNode.execute between the model response and the next loop iteration. Feeds the failure back to the model as a normal tool result, so the agent can pick a different tool or fix its arguments on the next turn. Otherwise a single bad tool name or a raising tool would abort the node and remove the model's chance to correct itself.

resilience.name: output schema validation
resilience.what_it_is: A node carrying NodeFlag.VALIDATE_OUTPUT has its structured output checked against node.output_schema after execution. _validate_against_schema supports Pydantic v2 (model_validate), Pydantic v1 (validate) and plain dict schemas with required keys. Violations are appended to result.guards_failed, a clean check appends "output_schema_validation" to result.guards_passed.
resilience.function_in_system: Runs in _post_execute_flags, after the node produced its output and before the transition is resolved. A deterministic, external check on model output that feeds the on_guard_fail edge, so a schema violation can be routed to a repair or retry node. Otherwise malformed structured output would flow into downstream nodes and fail there, far from its cause.

resilience.name: guard checks on node output
resilience.what_it_is: Guard objects exposing check_output are run against a node's raw output inside PromptNode.execute; each guard lands in result.guards_passed or, on a raised exception, in result.guards_failed. GuardNode is the standalone variant: it runs guards against a context key or the last message without an LLM call and routes to on_pass or on_fail.
resilience.function_in_system: Sits after the model call inside a node, and as its own node between two steps of the graph. Provides the guards_failed signal that on_guard_fail edges route on, and lets a graph gate progress on a content check before the output reaches the user or the next tool. Otherwise output violating a content or format rule would pass through unnoticed.

resilience.name: adversarial self-critique with severity routing
resilience.what_it_is: CritiqueNode is a PromptNode preconfigured with adversarial-review instructions asking the model for weaknesses, counter-arguments, improvements and a severity score between 0.0 and 1.0. When the parsed severity exceeds severity_threshold (default 0.5), the node routes to whichever of the transitions "revise", "improve", "retry" or "replan" is configured. A non-numeric severity degrades to 0.0.
resilience.function_in_system: Sits as its own node after an answering or planning node. Puts a second model pass between a draft and its acceptance, and turns the verdict into a routing decision back to a revision step. Otherwise a weak or flawed first answer would be returned as the final result with no review step.

resilience.name: message history trimming with system-message preservation
resilience.what_it_is: GraphState.trim_messages caps the message list at max_messages (default 200). It keeps every system message and fills the remainder with the most recent non-system messages, guaranteeing at least one kept non-system slot. The engine calls it after every node execution in both the blocking and the streaming path.
resilience.function_in_system: Runs in the state-update step of each traversal iteration. Bounds the prompt that every following model call carries, while protecting the instructions that define the agent's behavior. Otherwise a long tool loop would grow the history until the provider rejects the request for exceeding the context window.

def trim_messages(self) -> None:
    """Trim message history to ``max_messages`` if exceeded.

    Keeps all system messages (essential context) plus the most
    recent non-system messages to stay within the configured cap.
    """
    if self.max_messages <= 0 or len(self.messages) <= self.max_messages:
        return
    system_msgs = [
        m
        for m in self.messages
        if getattr(m, "type", None) == "system" or type(m).__name__ == "SystemMessage"
    ]
    non_system = [m for m in self.messages if m not in system_msgs]
    keep = self.max_messages - len(system_msgs)
    if keep < 1:
        keep = 1
    self.messages = system_msgs + non_system[-keep:]

resilience.name: node result caching with FIFO eviction
resilience.what_it_is: A node carrying NodeFlag.CACHEABLE gets a deterministic cache key: sha256 over the node name plus the JSON-serialized values of its declared input_keys, truncated to 32 characters. A hit returns a deep copy of the cached NodeResult with transition_reason="cache_hit" and skips execution entirely. Only error-free results are stored, and the cache evicts the oldest entry once it holds 128 entries.
resilience.function_in_system: Sits in _pre_execute_flags before execution and in _post_execute_flags after it. Skips repeated LLM calls for a node whose declared inputs have not changed, which matters in loops that revisit the same node. Refusing to cache failed results keeps a transient error from being replayed for the rest of the run. Otherwise every revisit would pay the full model call again.

resilience.name: LLM-based output summarization
resilience.what_it_is: A node carrying NodeFlag.SUMMARIZE_OUTPUT whose raw output exceeds 1000 characters gets an extra model call instructing the model to condense it while preserving facts, numbers and conclusions. The summary replaces result.raw_output. A failing summarization call is logged and leaves the original output in place.
resilience.function_in_system: Runs in _post_execute_flags, after the node produced its output and before it is passed on to the next node. Shrinks what a verbose step contributes to the context of every following step. The fallback to the original output keeps a failed summarization from losing the result. Otherwise a single long tool dump or analysis would occupy the context window for the rest of the run.

resilience.name: per-node context isolation
resilience.what_it_is: NodeFlag.NO_HISTORY strips the conversation from state.messages for the duration of one node, keeping a leading system message, and restores the original messages plus whatever the node added afterwards. NodeFlag.ISOLATED_CONTEXT replaces state.context with only the keys the node declares in input_keys, and merges back only the node's output_key and its automatic {name}_output entry.
resilience.function_in_system: Runs in _pre_execute_flags and _post_execute_flags around a single node execution. Gives a node a clean, minimal input so unrelated history cannot steer it, and keeps its intermediate scratch values out of the shared context. Otherwise every node would inherit the full accumulated history and context, which costs tokens and lets earlier reasoning bias a step meant to be independent.

def record_success(self) -> None:
    """Reset on success — model is healthy."""
    self.failures = 0
    self.state = "closed"

def record_failure(self) -> None:
    """Track failure. Open circuit after threshold."""
    self.failures += 1
    self.last_failure = time.monotonic()
    if self.failures >= self.failure_threshold:
        self.state = "open"
        logger.warning(
            "FallbackChain: circuit OPEN for %s after %d consecutive failures",
            self.model_id,
            self.failures,
        )

def should_skip(self) -> bool:
    """Check if this model should be skipped."""
    if self.state == "closed":
        return False
    if self.state == "open":
        # Check if recovery timeout has elapsed
        elapsed = time.monotonic() - self.last_failure
        if elapsed >= self.recovery_timeout:
            self.state = "half_open"
            logger.info(
                "FallbackChain: circuit HALF_OPEN for %s (testing recovery)",
                self.model_id,
            )
            return False  # Try once
        return True  # Still broken, skip
    # half_open — allow one attempt
    return False

@staticmethod
def _apply_redactions(text: str, findings: list[SecurityFinding]) -> str:
    """Replace detected spans with redaction labels.

    Processes findings in reverse order (right to left) so character
    offsets remain valid after each replacement.
    """
    # Sort by start position descending
    sorted_findings = sorted(findings, key=lambda f: f.start, reverse=True)
    result = text
    for f in sorted_findings:
        label = f"[{f.category.upper()}]"
        result = result[: f.start] + label + result[f.end :]
    return result

def classify_failure(error_type: str, error_message: str) -> FailureCategory:
    """Classify an error as infrastructure, strategy, or unknown.

    Deterministic — no LLM call.  Based on error type name and
    message pattern matching.

    Args:
        error_type: The exception class name.
        error_message: The error message text.

    Returns:
        The classified :class:`FailureCategory`.
    """
    # Check type name (strip module prefix)
    bare_type = error_type.rsplit(".", 1)[-1] if "." in error_type else error_type

    if bare_type in _INFRA_TYPES:
        return FailureCategory.INFRASTRUCTURE

    error_lower = error_message.lower()
    if any(p in error_lower for p in _INFRA_PATTERNS):
        return FailureCategory.INFRASTRUCTURE

    if bare_type in _STRATEGY_TYPES:
        return FailureCategory.STRATEGY
    if any(p in error_lower for p in _STRATEGY_PATTERNS):
        return FailureCategory.STRATEGY

    return FailureCategory.UNKNOWN

def _is_duplicate(self, file_path: str, event_type: str) -> bool:
        """Debounce: check if this event was recently emitted."""
        key = f"{event_type}:{file_path}"
        now = time.monotonic()

        last = self._recent_events.get(key)
        if last is not None and (now - last) < self._debounce_seconds:
            return True

        self._recent_events[key] = now

        # Garbage-collect old entries
        cutoff = now - self._debounce_seconds * 10
        self._recent_events = {k: v for k, v in self._recent_events.items() if v > cutoff}
        return False

async def handle(
    self,
    ctx: RequestContext,
    exc: Exception,
) -> MCPError | None:
    """Attempt to handle *exc*.

    Returns the ``MCPError`` produced by the matched handler,
    or ``None`` if no handler matched.
    """
    handler = self.find_handler(exc)
    if handler is None:
        return None

    import asyncio

    result = handler(ctx, exc)
    if asyncio.iscoroutine(result):
        result = await result

    if isinstance(result, MCPError):

    logger.warning(
        "Exception handler for %s returned %s instead of MCPError",
        type(exc).__name__,
        type(result).__name__,

    return None

def consume(self, key: str) -> tuple[bool, float]:
    """Try to consume one token from the bucket for *key*."""
    now = time.monotonic()
    with self._lock:
        tokens, last_time = self._buckets.get(key, (self._burst, now))

        # Refill tokens based on elapsed time
        elapsed = now - last_time
        tokens = min(self._burst, tokens + elapsed * self._rate)

        if tokens >= 1.0:
            self._buckets[key] = (tokens - 1.0, now)
            allowed, retry = True, 0.0
        else:
            deficit = 1.0 - tokens
            retry = deficit / self._rate if self._rate > 0 else 60.0
            self._buckets[key] = (tokens, now)
            allowed, retry = False, retry

        # Evict stale buckets periodically or when the map grows too large.
        # Remove entries not accessed in the last 5 minutes.
        _last_cleanup = getattr(self, "_last_cleanup", 0.0)
        if len(self._buckets) > self._MAX_BUCKETS or (
            now - _last_cleanup > 60.0 and len(self._buckets) > 100
        ):
            stale_cutoff = now - 300.0
            stale_keys = [k for k, (_, lt) in self._buckets.items() if lt < stale_cutoff]

                del self._buckets[k]
            self._last_cleanup = now  # type: ignore[attr-defined]

        return allowed, retry

def get(self, token: str) -> dict[str, Any] | None:
    """Return cached payload if valid, else ``None``.

    The read path is lock-free for performance under high concurrency.
    Python's GIL guarantees ``dict.get()`` atomicity.  Best-effort
    LRU reordering and expiry eviction are wrapped in try/except to
    tolerate benign races with concurrent ``put()`` calls.
    """
    entry = self._store.get(token)
    if entry is None:
        return None
    payload, cached_at = entry
    # Honour JWT expiry — evict if token has since expired
    exp = payload.get("exp")
    if exp is not None and exp < time.time():
        try:
            del self._store[token]
        except KeyError:
            pass  # Concurrent eviction — benign
        return None
    # Best-effort LRU reordering (race with put is harmless)
    try:
        self._store.move_to_end(token)
    except KeyError:
        pass  # Concurrent eviction — benign
    return payload

def put(self, token: str, payload: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
    """Cache a verified payload."""
    with self._lock:
        if token in self._store:
            self._store.move_to_end(token)
            self._store[token] = (payload, time.time())
            return
        if len(self._store) >= self._max_size:
            self._store.popitem(last=False)  # evict oldest
        self._store[token] = (payload, time.time())

        stored_prev = entry.get("prev_hash")
        if stored_prev != prev_hash:
            return False

        check_entry = {k: v for k, v in entry.items() if k != "hmac"}

resilience.name: circular cross-agent reference detection
resilience.what_it_is: resolve_cross_agents carries the set of already loaded file paths (_loading_chain). A referenced path that already appears in the set aborts loading with the full reference chain in the error. Recursive loading passes an extended copy of the chain to each level.
resilience.function_in_system: Runs while the peer network is loaded from .superagent files, before the peer agents are built. Otherwise agent files that reference each other send the loader into unbounded recursion.
